verses.modern: Still the LORD did not turn from the burning of His great wrath, by which His anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked him.

verses.kjv: And the LORD said, I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.
verses.modern: The LORD said, "I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel. I will cast off this city that I have chosen, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there."

verses.kjv: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.modern: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

verses.kjv: In his days Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates: and king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo, when he had seen him.
verses.modern: In his days Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up to the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates. King Josiah went to meet him, and Pharaoh Neco killed him at Megiddo, as soon as he saw him.

verses.kjv: And his servants carried him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in his own sepulchre. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father's stead.
verses.modern: His servants carried him dead in a chariot from Megiddo and brought him to Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb. And the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father's place.

verses.kjv: Jehoahaz was twenty and three years old when he began to reign; and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.modern: Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign. He reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

verses.kjv: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.modern: He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that His fathers had done.

verses.kjv: And Pharaohnechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and put the land to a tribute of an hundred talents of silver, and a talent of gold.
verses.modern: Pharaoh Neco put him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem, and laid on the land a tribute of a hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold.

verses.kjv: And Pharaohnechoh made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the room of Josiah his father, and turned his name to Jehoiakim, and took Jehoahaz away: and he came to Egypt, and died there.
verses.modern: Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the place of Josiah his father, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But he took Jehoahaz away. He came to Egypt and died there.

verses.kjv: And Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; but he taxed the land to give the money according to the commandment of Pharaoh: he exacted the silver and the gold of the people of the land, of every one according to his taxation, to give it unto Pharaohnechoh.
verses.modern: Jehoiakim gave the silver and the gold to Pharaoh. But he taxed the land to give the money according to the command of Pharaoh. He exacted the silver and the gold of the people of the land, from everyone according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Neco.

verses.kjv: Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign; and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Zebudah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
verses.modern: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign. He reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebidah the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.

verses.kjv: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his fathers had done.
verses.modern: He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that His fathers had done.

chapters.summary: Josiah read the Book of the Law before all the people, renewed the covenant, and destroyed the high places, altars, Asherah poles, and mediums throughout Judah. He celebrated a great Passover but was killed in battle against Pharaoh Neco at Megiddo.

verses.kjv: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years: then he turned and rebelled against him.
verses.modern: In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant for three years. Then he turned and rebelled against him.

verses.kjv: And the LORD sent against him bands of the Chaldees, and bands of the Syrians, and bands of the Moabites, and bands of the children of Ammon, and sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by his servants the prophets.
verses.modern: The LORD sent against Him bands of the Chaldeans and bands of the Syrians and bands of the Moabites and bands of the Ammonites, and sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word of the LORD that He spoke by His servants the prophets.

verses.kjv: Surely at the commandment of the LORD came this upon Judah, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he did;
verses.modern: Surely this came upon Judah at the command of the LORD, to remove them out of His sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he had done,

verses.kjv: And also for the innocent blood that he shed: for he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood; which the LORD would not pardon.
verses.modern: Also for the innocent blood that He had shed. For He filled Jerusalem with innocent blood. The LORD would not pardon.

verses.kjv: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.modern: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

verses.kjv: So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers: and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his stead.
verses.modern: So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place.

verses.kjv: And the king of Egypt came not again any more out of his land: for the king of Babylon had taken from the river of Egypt unto the river Euphrates all that pertained to the king of Egypt.
verses.modern: The king of Egypt did not come again out of his land, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt from the Brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates.

verses.kjv: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem three months. And his mother's name was Nehushta, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.
verses.modern: Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he became king. He reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father had done.
verses.modern: He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that His father had done.

verses.kjv: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
verses.modern: At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up to Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.

verses.kjv: And Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against the city, and his servants did besiege it.
verses.modern: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to the city while his servants were besieging it,

verses.kjv: And Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his servants, and his princes, and his officers: and the king of Babylon took him in the eighth year of his reign.
verses.modern: Jehoiachin the king of Judah gave himself up to the king of Babylon, himself and his mother and his servants and his officials and his palace officials. The king of Babylon took him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign

verses.kjv: And he carried out thence all the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king's house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of Israel had made in the temple of the LORD, as the LORD had said.
verses.modern: Carried off all the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold in the temple of the LORD, which Solomon king of Israel had made, as the LORD had foretold.

verses.kjv: And he carried away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valour, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and smiths: none remained, save the poorest sort of the people of the land.
verses.modern: He carried away all Jerusalem and all the officials and all the mighty men of valor, ten thousand captives. All the craftsmen and the smiths. None remained, except the poorest people of the land.

verses.kjv: And he carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon, and the king's mother, and the king's wives, and his officers, and the mighty of the land, those carried he into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.
verses.modern: He carried away Jehoiachin to Babylon. The king's mother, the king's wives, his officials, and the chief men of the land he took into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon.

verses.kjv: And all the men of might, even seven thousand, and craftsmen and smiths a thousand, all that were strong and apt for war, even them the king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon.
verses.modern: The king of Babylon brought captive to Babylon all the men of valor, 7,000, and the craftsmen and the metal workers, 1,000, all of them strong and fit for war.

verses.kjv: And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his father's brother king in his stead, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
verses.modern: The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his place, and changed his name to Zedekiah.

verses.kjv: Zedekiah was twenty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. And his mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
verses.modern: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king. He reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.

verses.kjv: And he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.
verses.modern: He did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.

verses.kjv: For through the anger of the LORD it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out from his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
verses.modern: For because of the anger of the LORD it came to the point in Jerusalem and Judah that He cast them out from His presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

chapters.summary: Jehoiakim served Nebuchadnezzar three years and then rebelled, bringing Babylon's wrath upon Judah. Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, carried away King Jehoiachin, the temple treasures, and 10,000 captives to Babylon, and made Zedekiah king.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, in the tenth day of the month, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he, and all his host, against Jerusalem, and pitched against it; and they built forts against it round about.
verses.modern: In the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with all his army against Jerusalem and laid siege to it. And they built siegeworks all around it.

verses.kjv: And the city was besieged unto the eleventh year of king Zedekiah.
verses.modern: So the city was besieged till the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

verses.kjv: And on the ninth day of the fourth month the famine prevailed in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.
verses.modern: On the ninth day of the fourth month the famine was so severe in the city that there was no food for the people of the land.

verses.kjv: And the city was broken up, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls, which is by the king's garden: (now the Chaldees were against the city round about:) and the king went the way toward the plain.
verses.modern: Then a breach was made in the city. All the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, by the king's garden, and the Chaldeans were around the city. And they went in the direction of the Arabah.

verses.kjv: And the army of the Chaldees pursued after the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army were scattered from him.
verses.modern: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho. All his army was scattered from him.

verses.kjv: So they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him.
verses.modern: Then they captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah. They passed sentence on him.

verses.kjv: And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.
verses.modern: They slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him in chains and took him to Babylon.

verses.kjv: And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which is the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem:
verses.modern: In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month—that was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, the captain of the bodyguard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: And he burnt the house of the LORD, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great man's house burnt he with fire.
verses.modern: He burned the house of the LORD and the king's house and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house He burned down.

verses.kjv: And all the army of the Chaldees, that were with the captain of the guard, brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
verses.modern: All the army of the Chaldeans, who were with the captain of the guard, broke down the walls around Jerusalem.

verses.kjv: Now the rest of the people that were left in the city, and the fugitives that fell away to the king of Babylon, with the remnant of the multitude, did Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carry away.
verses.modern: The rest of the people who were left in the city and the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, together with the rest of the crowd, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried into exile.

verses.kjv: But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen.
verses.modern: But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and plowmen.

verses.kjv: And the pillars of brass that were in the house of the LORD, and the bases, and the brasen sea that was in the house of the LORD, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon.
verses.modern: The pillars of bronze that were in the house of the LORD, and the stands and the bronze sea that were in the house of the LORD, the Chaldeans broke in pieces and carried the bronze to Babylon.

verses.kjv: And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away.
verses.modern: They took away the pots and the shovels and the snuffers and the dishes for incense and all the vessels of bronze used in the temple service,

verses.kjv: And the firepans, and the basons, and such things as were of gold, in gold, and of silver, in silver, the captain of the guard took away.
verses.modern: The fire pans also and the basins. What was of gold the captain of the guard took away as gold, and what was of silver, as silver.

verses.kjv: The two pillars, one sea, and the bases which Solomon had made for the house of the LORD; the brass of all these vessels was without weight.
verses.modern: As for the two pillars, the one sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these vessels was beyond weight.

verses.kjv: The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and the chapiter upon it was brass: and the height of the chapiter three cubits; and the wreathen work, and pomegranates upon the chapiter round about, all of brass: and like unto these had the second pillar with wreathen work.
verses.modern: The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and on it was a capital of bronze. The height of the capital was three cubits. A latticework and pomegranates, all of bronze, were all around the capital. And the second pillar had the same, with the latticework.

verses.kjv: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:
verses.modern: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold;

verses.kjv: And out of the city he took an officer that was set over the men of war, and five men of them that were in the king's presence, which were found in the city, and the principal scribe of the host, which mustered the people of the land, and threescore men of the people of the land that were found in the city:
verses.modern: From the city he took an officer who had been in command of the men of war, and five men of the king's council who were found in the city. The secretary of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land. Sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.

verses.kjv: And Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took these, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah:
verses.modern: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

verses.kjv: And the king of Babylon smote them, and slew them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away out of their land.
verses.modern: The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was taken into exile out of its land.

verses.kjv: And as for the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler.
verses.modern: Over the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, governor.

verses.kjv: And when all the captains of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, there came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Careah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.
verses.modern: Now when all the captains of the forces in the open country and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah governor, they came with their men to Gedaliah at Mizpah, namely, Ishmael the son of Netaniah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite.

verses.kjv: And Gedaliah sware to them, and to their men, and said unto them, Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon; and it shall be well with you.
verses.modern: Gedaliah swore to them and their men, saying, "Do not be afraid because of the Chaldean officials. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon. It will be well with you."

verses.kjv: But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah.
verses.modern: But in the seventh month, Ishmael the son of Netaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal family, came with ten men and struck down Gedaliah and put him to death along with the Jews and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

verses.kjv: And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose, and came to Egypt: for they were afraid of the Chaldees.
verses.modern: Then all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the forces arose and went to Egypt, for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

verses.kjv: And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, that Evilmerodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;
verses.modern: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, graciously freed Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison.

verses.kjv: And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon;
verses.modern: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the kings who were with him in Babylon.

verses.kjv: And changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.
verses.modern: So Jehoiachin put off his prison garments. And every day of his life he dined regularly at the king's table,

verses.kjv: And his allowance was a continual allowance given him of the king, a daily rate for every day, all the days of his life.
verses.modern: For his allowance, a regular allowance was given him by the king, according to his daily needs, as long as he lived.

chapters.summary: Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon, and Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem for two years until famine overwhelmed the city. The temple was burned, the walls torn down, and the people carried into exile; Gedaliah was appointed governor but was assassinated, and the remnant fled to Egypt.
